text:
matt: Morning — need a quick quota ask for europe-west4. We're hitting both GPU quota and secondary IP range exhaustion when trying to create a high-density node pool for inference (A100s). Can someone confirm the best ask to put to GCP?

alex: Which quotas exactly? GPU (accelerator quota), or VPC subnet secondary range / alias IPs?

matt: Both. Error when provisioning nodepool: 
```
ERROR: Insufficient IP addresses in subnet for pods. required: 120, available: 24
node provisioning failed: acceleratorQuotasExceeded: Requested 8 A100s but only 2 available in project
```

jiwon: Oof. Region is europe-west4 (wdc-equivalent). For our packing plan we want 30 pods/node with pod density optimizations (maxPods=110 on small nodes is not possible because CNI/default max pods calc). We need to increase secondary IP range size for the GKE cluster and accelerator quota to 20 A100s to support ramp.

priya: Recommended GCP request payload: ask for Accelerator quota (A100 80GB or A100 40GB?) and 'VPC: Expand secondary range in subnet eu-west4-subnet-ml to /20' so we get more alias IPs for pods. Also ask to raise 'GKE max pods per node' soft-limit? (that's config but eligibility depends on CNI).

matt: We're using gke standard with VPC-native (alias IP). Nodepool: 8x A100-80 nodes initially, 30 pods per node. We need headroom for burst + canary autoscaling. Can we ask GCP for: accelerator quota = +20 A100-80GB, secondary IP range additional /22 for that cluster's subnet, and project-level 'VM instances' CPU quota bump in eu-west4?

maya: I'm +1 on A100-80 increase. For IPs, GCP tends to prefer you either expand the secondary range or create a new secondary range and attach to the subnetwork. Request text I used before: 
"Please increase the size of the secondary IP range 'gke-eu4-pods' from /24 to /20 for subnetwork projects/our-project/regions/europe-west4 to allow higher pod density node pools. Also increase the GPU (A100 80GB) quota in europe-west4 from 4 to 24."

alex: Also call out CNI maxPods calc. GKE uses kubenet vs VPC-native; our clusters are VPC-native. If they expand the secondary range, we can set max-pods-per-node via node pool config. We'll need to update node pool creation YAML to set --max-pods-per-node=64 when creating custom CNI? Suggest include planned nodepool YAML snippet so support sees it's not a misconfig.

matt: Good idea. Snippet I plan to include: 
```yaml
apiVersion: container.cnrm.cloud.google.com/v1beta1
kind: ContainerNodePool
metadata:
  name: high-density-inference
spec:
  initialNodeCount: 8
  config:
    machineType: n1-standard-32
    accelerators:
    - acceleratorType: nvidia-tesla-a100
      acceleratorCount: 1
    oauthScopes: []
  maxPodsConstraint:
    maxPodsPerNode: 30
  autoscaling:
    minNodeCount: 2
    maxNodeCount: 24
```

jiwon: That looks fine. Also include that we'll create a dedicated subnet for this cluster if they recommend it; gives isolation. For the accelerator quota increase, include use case: low-latency inference serving for enterprise customers with SLA, production traffic expected ~200 qps and warm KV cache requiring reserved capacity.

priya: I'll open the internal support ticket and draft the GCP quota request. Quick checks: are we ok with temporary workaround to shard nodepools across two smaller subnets to buy time?

matt: Yes, we can shard as a mitigation: new nodepool in europe-west4-b with separate secondary range, then migrate workloads via nodeAffinity and a rollout. But long-term better to expand range.

gcp-support-bot: Ticket created: Q-2026-5284. Requested: A100-80 quota increase to 24 (region europe-west4), expand secondary IP range 'gke-eu4-pods' to /20, and increase CPUs in region by 200. GCP response ETA ~ 48-72 hours.

maya: Thanks — once they confirm I'll queue the nodepool create in staging and run a smoke test with a canary group of 50 pods.

alex: One more note: mention expected NAT egress capacity; if we increase pod counts per node we might also need more NAT IPs per region to hit egress SLOs. Add that to the ticket as "possible additional NAT capacity".

matt: Good catch. I'll update the ticket description with NAT headroom and a statement that we'll create a fallback smaller-pool policy for burst traffic.

priya: Updated ticket Q-2026-5284 with NAT note and attach nodepool YAML + traffic profile. Will post updates here when GCP responds. :thumbsup:

matt: Awesome — thanks everyone.
